headline: Profit rises on lower taxes, but debt keeps climbing
summary_short: PG&E reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5,902M, essentially flat y/y (+0.1%) but down 14.2% q/q; net income rose 38.6% y/y to $761M on a sharply lower tax provision, and diluted EPS climbed to $0.33 from $0.24 a year ago, though both eased back from a stronger first quarter.
summary_long: Revenue of $5,902M was flat y/y — $201M more electricity-cost pass-through offset by $180M less interim WMCE rate relief — and fell 14.2% q/q. Operating income rose 15.2% y/y to $1,263M as O&M expense fell 11%, outpacing higher electricity costs. Net income climbed 38.6% y/y to $761M, boosted by a $100M drop in the tax provision (effective rate -7.8%) from generation-related deductions; diluted EPS rose to $0.33 from $0.24. Cash of $972M nearly doubled y/y but fell q/q. Long-term debt rose to $61,768M as PG&E funds its $12.4B 2026 capex plan with debt, not new equity.

drivers.explanation: Q2 revenue was roughly flat y/y: about $201M more cost-of-electricity pass-through revenue was largely offset by roughly $180M less interim rate relief under the 2023 WMCE proceeding.

Y/y growth reflects an 11% ($317M) drop in operating & maintenance expense, mostly from $180M less previously-deferred WMCE expense recognized in the prior-year quarter, outpacing higher pass-through electricity costs.

The income tax provision fell $100M y/y in Q2, driven by increased deductions for costs attributable to electric generation, pushing the effective tax rate to -7.8% and lifting net income faster than operating income.
EPS growth tracks net income: the same generation-related tax deductions that cut the tax provision also boosted income available to common shareholders.

Six-month interest expense rose 4% y/y due to the issuance of additional long-term debt, as PG&E funds its 2026 capex plan (est. $12.4B) via debt while planning no common equity issuance through 2030.
Equity growth is explained by six-month net income available to common ($1,591M) exceeding common and preferred dividends declared over the same period.

The approved 2023 WMCE final decision continues to flow into results, while wildfire-fund amortization (accelerated on SCE's Eaton Fire disclosure) and ongoing rate-case proceedings remain the key forward risks.
